titles.546: a bucket that pools SEVERAL field points is not a field group: the mirrored second arm arrived as one index carrying all 318 rays from three field points, so its least-squares waist measured the IMAGE HEIGHT (3865 um) and drew the focus plane 95.35 mm out while the mirror-image arm -- identical |m| to six digits -- read -0.02 mm; the decomposition is now recovered from the launch points instead of a collapsible upstream index (0757)
titles.547: an informational readout must never take the solve down with it: bugs/0755's 'what field WOULD land' snapshot was called unconditionally at the top of _apply_conjugate_pair, so a consumer composing only part of the service raised AttributeError and the entire conjugate solve died (penta 412) -- the snapshot is now guarded, and the guard composes services with the helper absent and raising to prove the solve survives (0758)
titles.548: the imaging group on one motor and the lens on another, as the bench is built: booking the image-side correction by sliding the SENSOR spends camera-to-mirror clearance and capped the device at 48.4-56.1 mm, while moving the whole group changes the track without spending any (mirror-to-sensor held 55.385-55.412 mm across 70.75 mm of travel) -- and the fold mirror's seat ALONE does nothing, because the fold walk lengthens mirror->sensor by exactly what the seat move shortens lens->mirror (0759)
titles.549: the filter travels with the imaging group, and 'already delivered' means the image LANDS: Motor 1 wrote only the mirror seat and the sensor standoff, so the filter rode the lens chain and ended 55.7 mm from the mirror it travels with (it needs a PAIR, like the lens -- writing one gap alone threw the sensor 259 mm out), and the idempotence test compared magnification alone, declaring a scene finished with the image 6.276 mm off the sensor (0761)
titles.550: 'already delivered' needs BOTH the first order and the MEASURED focus to say the image lands -- gating on the first order alone (0761) let a scene whose traced image sat 5.932 mm in front of the sensor be declared finished and locked there; plus the solve banner now sits beside the system HUD, offset by the HUD's own rendered width (vtkTextActor.GetSize takes an OUTPUT array -- the one-argument form raised and silently left it stacked) (0762)
titles.551: the focus snap may not leave the scene worse than it found it: _traced_bundle_best_focus_shift matched only the LEGACY termination spelling, so on a scene whose builder stamps 'image' (om05a: 644 rays land as 'image', 0 as 'target_termination') it returned None on every call -- which the snap reads as 'no bundle measurable' and answers with an unverified station-frame single shot, moving the sensor +5.8819 mm off a focus the solve had just landed at -0.0506 mm; the measure now accepts both spellings and the unfrozen branch measures the traced defocus before and after and restores the rows when the move made it worse (bugs/0577's rule was frozen-branch-only) (0764)
titles.552: 'land it' is a question about the PIXEL, not about millimetres: the focus banner told the user to move the device stage with the image 0.05058 mm off and a 1.51 um blur on a 4.5 um pixel -- a third of a pixel, nothing left to move -- because the gate was a hardcoded 0.05 mm that the residual cleared by 0.6 um; the instruction now compares the traced blur to the pixel pitch (smaller side of a rectangular pixel), which is the same criterion the bench's own DOF spec uses (86/195/410 um at f/5.6 all back-solve to c ~ 4.7 um) (0767)
titles.553: a camera stage declared on the WRONG row must say so: _image_write_locked_by_vendor_hardware exempts the stage only when its row IS the row the solve writes, so om05a_folded's stage on the mirror row fell through to the same bare 'the sensor carries the vendor camera body' line a scene with NO stage gets -- Motor 1 skipped, 7.31 mm reported, nothing pointing at the cause; the reason now names both rows, and the lock still refuses to re-point itself at the write row because that row may be a vendor body (pointing it at a desp-placed LED panel satisfied the first order to -5e-13 while the trace stayed 7.31 mm out) (0769)
titles.554: MOTOR 1 must be SHOWN to have moved the sensor or not move at all: the seat is written in desp_x while the pad is written as a THICKNESS, which advances along whatever direction the chain points after the fold -- those coincide on om05a_folded_80mm (a -10 mm request moves the sensor exactly (-10,0,0)) and do not on om05a_folded, whose mirror 2 carries tilt_y 90 / tilt_z 180 and throws the sensor (-10,+20,0), |d| 22.36 for 10 mm of intent; the first order books stations so it reported a clean 1.0000 gain while the traced focus moved 0.4142 of the request, and the solve wrote geometry that looked solved and was not -- the move now measures the sensor before and after and reverts every field it wrote, carry pair included (0770)
titles.555: a ROW that cannot absorb a move is not a MACHINE with no room: FOV 20 on a 20x20x1 device needs the lens 136.97 mm along its leg against a 130.889 mm gap, so the thickness pair would drive the row negative and the mover refused with 'the gap would go negative' -- which reads as 'no room' while the mover's own physical probe reported 155.79 mm and the STEP bodies still had 19.85 mm of clearance at the cap; the refusal now records the shortfall (so bugs/0573's make-room path has a number instead of silently never running) and names the physical room and that the limit is the row partition, with the physical-room refusal above it untouched (0771)
titles.556: a hardware rail must not move when the lens moves: a 23x23x1 device left the image 77.2 mm off with a 1970 um spot because MOTOR 1 needed to travel to 192.0 mm against a hand-guessed floor of 192.683 -- a 0.66 mm miss -- while the authored A5+C1 geometry gives a rail of [138.231, 286.630]; with it the same case lands at 191.979 with 644 rays, -0.081 mm and a 2.10 um spot. bugs/0766's derivation was worse than the guess it replaced because it read the LIVE gaps (a5 and c1 track the LENS, not the arm: mid-solve it produced [258.9, 407.3]), so it now reports only the invariant rail LENGTH and the row indices, and leaves the limits to the scene (0772)
titles.557: 'already delivered' must ask EVERY formed image, not one of them: a 21x21x1 device reported 'the lens did not move -- the field was already delivered' with Face A 3.025 mm off (419 um spot) and Face B 0.09958 mm off, because the gate read the TOP-LEVEL offset_mm which carried face B's number, a hair inside the 0.1 mm tolerance -- bugs/0752 split the measurement per image precisely so one arm could not speak for the other, and this gate never asked; whichever image is worst now decides, the same rule bugs/0764's snap guard states (0773)
titles.558: a field that overflows the sensor must be SAID, not silently clipped: the user noticed the two image strips migrating outward and asked whether it was accounted for -- it was not, a ray reaching the detector PLANE but landing beyond its active area counted as landing while the banner reported focus and spot as usual; two laws now govern it, |u|outer = 9.278*|m| (position) and |v|half = device*|m|/2 (length), verified to +-0.005 mm over two device sizes and five magnifications, and the check PREDICTS the extent because counting landings under-reports badly (a 30 mm device at FOV 24 registers 44 rays 0.005 mm out while 2.88 mm per side is lost and only 80% of the part is imaged) (0774)
titles.559: measure the delivered magnification from the RAYS and check the claim: the banner's '|m| 1.045' could not be contradicted by anything, because every readout that might have came from the same first order that produced it -- bugs/0774's LAW 2 reads backwards into |m| = 2*|v|half/device, which is scene-independent (unlike the strip POSITION, whose 9.278 coefficient is one bench's arm offset and would be a hardcoded scene constant); quiet on the measured cases to 0.03% against a 2% threshold, skipped when the strip is clipped because a clipped strip under-reports its own length (0775)
titles.560: the split-field arm offset is the SCENE's to declare, like camera_focus_stage: the strip-POSITION law |centre| = k*|m| needs k, the object-space half-separation of the two arms' axes (8.778 mm on om05a_folded_80mm), which is a property of the BENCH and would bake one machine's geometry into the simulator if hardcoded; it round-trips through save/load with every malformed value DROPPED including non-finite (1e400 -> inf passes a bare '>0' test and pformat writes it back as the bare token `inf`, so the .py fails to import and both loaders fall back to surfaces-only, silently discarding every persisted setting), and the check is inert on any scene that declares nothing (0776)
titles.561: focus groups follow the LAUNCH POINT so the two arms of a split field agree: one arm read a ~400 um waist and the other sub-micron on a bench whose bodies are symmetric to 35 nm and whose traced bundles mirror about z=-25 to max|mirror(A)-B| = 0.0 -- identical rays giving two answers, which can only be the readout; field_index is a uniform ray-index division over a RAGGED launch (corner probes make some fields 5 rays and others 361) and arm B's boundaries landed 20 rays out of step, inventing a 0.98 um 'sharp field' that then disqualified that arm's real 400 um fields via the bugs/0753 waist<=10*sharpest test. Grouping on the physical launch point makes the arms agree to 0.01 um, and reveals that at device 21 BOTH arms are 419 um blurred -- arm B's sub-micron waists were fiction (0778)
titles.562: stray light that reached the sensor by another optical route is not the image: on om05a_folded_80mm the same 9 launch rays per arm that stop at the aperture stop at device 23 clear the centre RA mirror's edge at device 21, cross the prism gap into the other arm's cube and back, and land 1.4 mm outside the strip; sharing their field's launch point they joined its focus group, and ONE dragged a 105-ray field's waist from 2.06 um to 656 um -- the whole '419 um blur' at device 21 and the FOV limit it implied for a 15 mm device. Landing rays now split per source into image-forming routes (>= 20% of the source's landings) and stray; focus groups key on launch point AND route, discreteness is decided per source, the overflow check and the drawn strips use the image only, and the banner names stray light that lands outside the image. The guard drives the real measurement on a synthetic mirrored split field and shows the same rays DO drag the waist without route data (0779)
titles.563: stray light that reached the sensor by another optical route draws FAINT: after bugs/0779 the banner correctly read 'Landed' and 'STRAY LIGHT: 6 ray(s) ... outside the image', yet the scene drew those cross-arm rays exactly like image light and the user flagged 'I still see many stray rays flying around'. They are real traced light, so per the bugs/0530 doctrine they are weighted, not hidden: each draw classifies its landing rays with the same split_stray_routes rule the focus measurement uses -- over the whole bundle, before the draw budget thins it -- and both scene draw loops multiply a stray ray's opacity by bugs/0604's ghost floor (0.15), leave its terminal status and drawn geometry untouched, and drop it from the Normal-to-Sensor view (bugs/0606), which shows the image (0780)
titles.564: one Solve FOV may not trace the same scene twice: profiled on om05a (21x21x1, 3D window open) Solve FOV took 237.8 s, 163.6 s of it in four full traces that were all focus measurements -- the finisher's before (bugs/0490), the snap's before and after (bugs/0764), the finisher's after -- and an independent review showed the snap's before re-traced the scene the finisher had just traced and, on a reverted snap, the finisher's after traced it a third time. A content fingerprint of every trace input the solve can write (rows, saved settings minus the image strips a trace writes, STEP offsets, scene sources, learned fold corrections, sampling mode) now lets a measured value be handed forward only while nothing changed: 2 traces instead of 4 on both the revert and the keep path, the focus readout restored after a revert, a stand-alone snap still measuring before and after, and no reuse at all with energy probability on, a fold relearn pending or a forced preview sampling (0781)
titles.565: MOTOR 1 must move the imaging group along the BEAM on any frame: the user said the production om05a has exactly the 80 mm build's two motors, but bugs/0770 had made its Motor 1 refuse because the move threw the sensor (-10, +20, 0) for a -10 mm request. Measured per +1 mm write, the standoff and the filter carry pair are chain thicknesses that move along the beam identically on both frames, while the seat's desp_x is a WORLD axis whose sign flips on the mirrored production frame (lens leg -x): +delta moved RA mirror 2 toward the object while the thicknesses moved the standoff and filter away. The seat is now written with a sign MEASURED by a restored +1 mm nudge projected on the lens leg, the solve's stage bound uses the same sign, and the bugs/0770 check also refuses a sensor that travels the right distance the wrong way. The real production move now carries sensor, mirror and filter exactly -10.000 mm along the beam; the 80 mm writes are bit-identical (0782)
titles.566: a device-size change at a fixed FOV restores the working distance, and the banner says what moved: the user saw 'the lens did not move' while changing device size ('the WD cannot be right without lens moving') and stated the bench's model -- three FOVs, each one WD and one image distance, one motor restores the WD. Two defects produced the banner: the solve summary read the lens move only from the vendor-lock residual, so every clean MOTOR 1 booking reported no move, and bugs/0727's already-delivered gate never asked the object side (om05a 80 mm at FOV 54: a 50 -> 49 mm device left the first order asking for a -0.883 mm lens move while the gate said nothing to move). Now, at an operating point (the image distance already this FOV's), a size change is ONE rigid move -- lens pair by object_delta, MOTOR 1 by object_delta + image_delta, stage bound checked first, every row put back on a MOTOR 1 refusal -- with no conjugate re-solve and no trace; on the real 80 mm scene 50 -> 40 lands on exactly the traced full solve's geometry (A5 125.5068, standoff 4.3213). The full solve records its lens move from whichever branch booked it (0783)
titles.567: the lens gap's floor is the METAL, not the row: the user measured the bench's own A5 dimension (the A5 gap reads 32.96 mm at a 22 mm device, 28.1 mm at 20 mm) and was right -- the lens block's position is booked as rows[front-1].thickness, which may not go negative, and on om05a_folded_80mm that zero sits 26.90 mm short of metal contact because the 50 mm prism's folded glass path is booked entirely on the outgoing leg while only ~25.29 mm of it runs along that leg in world. A 0.5 mm device at FOV 23 was refused short by 5.099 mm with 155.8 mm of PHYSICAL room left (bugs/0771 deferred exactly this). _recover_lens_leg_headroom now shifts the shortfall out of the nearest upstream AIR gap into the lens gap and compensates every body in between on its OWN measured desp frame, reverting unless every world pose is provably unchanged: 0.5 mm at FOV 23 solves and lands at 2.28 um with 19.8 mm of clearance, 20 mm at FOV 21 lands at 2.47 um, 22 mm at auto FOV is unchanged to every digit (2.22 um, room 30.9/64.4), and 0.5 mm at FOV 17 still refuses on the physical gate (0784)
titles.568: a datasheet the app cannot read is a vendor it cannot import: the user asked why every newly-introduced camera brand failed to import and whether it could read the PDF text at all (error.png, the Hikrobot MV-CH120-60UM, whose sheet states Pixel size 3.45 um and Resolution 4096 x 3000 in plain text). It can -- the SHARED extract_pdf_text, used by the camera folder importer and the machine-vision lens importer alike, had three defects, none brand-specific: the raw-literal fallback harvested PDF plumbing (one /Lang (en-US) marked-content property per run -- 380 on that sheet, 2738 on the Bopixel BC-Gx25M12X4 -- glued between every label and its value, defeating every Label-colon-value regex); a show-string whose font carried no ToUnicode was DROPPED, so a sheet mixing fonts inside one spec row lost half of every row (the CMap pass returned 5 ASCII letters, the literal pass had 'Pixel size' with no pitch after it), and the printability test had to count Latin-1 160..255 or the row's own U+00D7 separator went with it; and the stdlib decoder understands a slice of PDF rather than the format, so a real parser now competes with it and the stdlib wins ties, keeping every existing scrape byte-identical. pdfminer's (cid:N) placeholders are discounted before that comparison ('cid' is three ASCII letters; the ELS-85 sheet is 1101 of them over the real 447). Measured: the flagged folder imports at 14.1312 x 10.3500 mm (4096 x 3.45 and 3000 x 3.45 exactly, via bugs/0307's pitch x resolution derivation, which never got the chance before), the Bopixel spec sheet parses on its own so its hand-written sidecar is no longer required, and across all 29 camera+lens datasheets under attachment/ the corpus goes 23 -> 25 with ZERO regressions and ZERO value changes (0785)
titles.569: a spec table is a table, and the sheet checks its own arithmetic: the user corrected bugs/0785's write-up -- 'WWK10-110CP-111V3: the magnification is on the first row in the datasheet table' -- and was right; the claim that the sheet stated no magnification had been made from flattened text without looking at the page, which shows Magnification (x) 1.0, Working Distance (mm) 110+-2, Mount C and Length (mm) 152.6. Two things stood in the way: that table is a raster IMAGE (pdfplumber sees 212 character objects on the page and only 26 in the top 62%, exactly the title and the word Datasheet), and even with perfect text bugs/0653's telecentric derivation refused it, because four of its six gates were written for the Edmund title format and missed on typography alone (it wanted '1.0X' and 'Mount: C-Mount' and the title's '110mm WD'/'1X'). The wording now reads a TABLE, and bugs/0565's corroboration is earned either the old way or from the sheet's own printed total -- 'Length of I/O (mm) 280+-2' with its note 'Length of I/O = WD + Length + Back Focal Length', which IS wd+length+flange: 110+152.6+17.526 = 280.126 against a printed 280. Checking the vendor's arithmetic beats matching their typography, and it is what makes OCR safe to feed in -- ocrmypdf --force-ocr reads '110+-2' as '1102', whose total of 1272 mm the sheet refutes itself, so the import refuses instead of shipping a 1102 mm working distance. Measured: clean table text -> effl 70.0315 (T/4 = 70.032), six mutants refuse, the Edmund route is untouched, and the whole 29-datasheet corpus shows zero regressions and zero value changes. No OCR digit-repair heuristic was added, and none should be (0786)
titles.570: when the spec table is a picture, read the picture -- but never trust it alone: the WWK10-110CP-111V3 lens folder still refused ('the datasheet PDF did not yield an effective focal length') after bugs/0785 and 0786, because there is no text to read -- 212 character objects on the page, 26 of them in the top 62% where the tables are, and those 26 are the title. _extract_pdf_text_ocr rasterises and recognises the pages, wired as a LAST resort so a readable datasheet never pays for it, cached under attachment/cad_cache/datasheet_ocr, and returning empty (the importer refusing exactly as before) when pdftoppm/tesseract are absent. Two measured choices: --psm 4, because this sheet prints two spec tables side by side and --psm 6 merges them so 'Magnification (x)' loses its 1.0 to the Field-of-View row; and pdftoppm -r 300 for the raster, because the tolerance glyph decides everything -- at 300 dpi '110+-2' survives as '110+2' so the regex stops at 110, while ocrmypdf --force-ocr rasterises differently and reads the same cell as '1102', a 1102 mm working distance. OCR output still has to earn bugs/0786's corroboration against the sheet's own printed total before it is used, which is what makes reading a picture safe: the 1102 misread totals 1272 against a printed 280 and would refuse. Measured: the folder now builds a surrogate in ~8 s with effl 70.0315, WD 110.0, span 152.6, F/7 and its STEP body; with OCR switched off the same folder refuses, on the original AND on the user's pdf-prep output (whose 3 MB of extracted text still contains no Magnification row, because pdf-prep's run_ocr hardcodes ocrmypdf --skip-text); whole 29-datasheet corpus shows zero regressions and zero value changes (0787)
titles.571: two OCR engines with complementary weaknesses, tried in turn: the user asked for a better offline deep-learning OCR and for rapidocr-onnxruntime in devenv.nix. It IS better and it is NOT a replacement -- measured on the COOLENS spec table, rapidocr keeps the glyph that decides the value ('110+-2' with the real character, where tesseract gives '110+2' and ocrmypdf's rasteriser gives '1102') and returns a BOX per line so a label pairs with its value by geometry instead of by --psm 4 luck, and it needs no external binary at all because pdfplumber rasterises in process; but its detector misses isolated one-character cells, so the row 'Best Aperture (F/#) | 7 ... Mount | C' comes back with the labels and neither value, and a missing mount means no flange and no derivation -- preferring it outright sent WWK10-110CP-111V3 back to refusing. So ocr_text_candidates offers each engine's reading best-first, cached under its own key, and the CALLER keeps the first that yields a usable result, which after bugs/0786 means the first that also passes corroboration against the sheet's own printed total. Merging the two texts was rejected: a regex would take whichever number appeared first and silently mix two engines' readings of one cell. _ocr_engine_available is the master switch and is consulted BEFORE the cache, so turning OCR off gives the pre-0787 refusal rather than a stale reading. Measured: the folder imports at effl 70.0315 in ~10 s cold, and the 29-datasheet corpus goes 23 -> 26 with zero regressions and zero value changes (0788)
titles.572: the image circle sizes the glass, under whatever name the vendor gave it: the user built a scene from the two folders bugs/0785-0788 made importable and asked whether the lens surrogate could fit the barrel of the STEP file, because it seemed too small to be true -- it could not. The COOLENS WWK10-110CP-111V3 surrogate came out with 14.0063 mm elements, exactly 1.4x its 10.0045 mm stop (the on-axis pupil footprint and nothing else), inside a barrel whose STEP measures 44.00 mm across, for a lens whose own datasheet row reads Max Sensor Size in phi-mm of 18.0. bugs/0662's rule was already right -- a finite-conjugate lens's front and rear glass must cover the FIELD, max(1.4*stop, image_circle + stop) = 28.0045 mm here, agreeing with the DWG's internal 30/31/34 mm bores -- but it never fired because cardinals.image_circle was None, and that was a FILING problem: the scrape lived in two places with different spelling lists, and the telecentric path (which this sheet takes) knew only the Edmund Maximum Image Circle spelling. One helper now holds every spelling, tolerating the phi that an OCR'd sheet renders as at-sign or registered-P, bounded to a plausible 1-400 mm; an image circle sizes apertures and, unlike the EFL, cannot move the first order. Measured: image circle 18.0, front and rear aperture 14.0063 -> 28.0045, effl and span unchanged, and the whole 29-datasheet corpus shows zero regressions and zero value changes. The scene's other banner -- field reaches the sensor edge, 66.5 percent of landing rays outside the active area -- is arithmetic, not a fault: a field defined as a DISC of the sensor diagonal (17.5157 mm) overflows the 14.1312 by 10.35 mm rectangle by exactly 17.5157/2 - 14.1312/2 = 1.6924 mm, which is what the trace reports, with a focus offset of -1.6e-11 mm (0789)
titles.573: read the vendor DWG, and refuse for the right reason: the user asked whether the SPO TCL4.0X-65DI-5M had a DWG file, and whether the 4X lens was settled. It does, and it is the right source -- 814 objects including 53 MTEXT entities WITH COORDINATES, so a label pairs with the value in its own row by geometry, with no recognition step. Neither earlier route could reach it: the PDF flattens the title block so every label is orphaned from its value (bugs/0565's failure mode, 314 characters of labels only) and OCR recovers the labels but not the small isolated value cells (bugs/0788's: rapidocr returns Optical Mgnification with no 4.0X, tesseract returns 14 characters for the whole drawing). Every number is corroborated before use: the magnification against the field row and the format it names (2.2 x 4.0 = 8.8 = the 2/3 inch width), the F-number against the numerical aperture (m/(2 NA) = 4.0/0.32 = 12.5), the working distance against the dimension run's own WD65, and the flange against the C-mount standard 17.526 -- which is also how the run is IDENTIFIED rather than guessed, since a run ending in anything but a standard flange is not a chain. The lens STILL does not import, and that is the finding: 65 + 142.5 + 17.526 = 225.026 mm of track, whose coincident-principal-plane focal length 36.0042 mm puts the front principal 19.99 mm IN FRONT of the housing, which bugs/0647's registration law rejects. With HH' unstated the sheet pins the TRACK and not the focal length, so no EFL is invented; the refusal now names the chain it read and what is missing instead of blaming a PDF that was never the problem (0790)
titles.574: a CAD title block is typeset ROTATED, so read it that way: the user supplied an OCR'd copy of the SPO TCL4.0X-65DI-5M drawing and asked whether it helped. It did not -- its text layer is the original's, 315 characters against 314, and neither states a focal length -- but checking it found the real cause of a failure worked around since bugs/0565. A drawing's title block is typeset at 90 degrees and a reading-order extractor walks it the wrong way, emitting every label in one run and every value in another, so no label-colon-value regex can pair them and a sheet that states its whole spec table reads as though it states nothing. Measured: all 284 characters on that page report upright=False and share just 20 distinct x0 values. _extract_pdf_text_layout assembles from character POSITIONS, swapping the axes when the page is rotated, grouping rows with one tolerance per page from the median glyph size, and separating words by comparing each gap against that glyph's OWN set width -- which for a rotated glyph is bottom minus top, not x1 minus x0. All three were learned the hard way: a per-character tolerance splits a label whose glyphs differ in size, a nominal-size gap glues Optical to Mgnification, and the line's median advance splits the wide ones. From the ORIGINAL PDF, with no OCR and no DWG, it now yields Optical Mgnification 4.0X, W.D(mm) 65, F/# 12.5 and N.A 0.16 on their own rows. Offered as a candidate ahead of the OCR engines, after the ordinary text layer, so nothing that already worked changes: the 29-datasheet corpus shows zero regressions and zero value changes and an upright PYRITE sheet still parses at effl 82.39 (0791)
titles.575: a catalogue states the conjugates, so solve for the LENS: the user confirmed no vendor releases a prescription unless you are their number one customer, so the importer has to work from catalogue data. f(2+m+1/m) + HH-prime = track is one equation in two unknowns, and bugs/0653 closed it by assuming coincident principal planes -- right near 1x and false above it. Measured: a 4x lens at 65 mm working distance needs a 325 mm track for that assumption, where Edmund's own 62-793 has 192.5 and the SPO TCL4.0X has 225, so the derived front principal plane lands in front of the barrel and bugs/0647's registration law refuses. No thick lens rescues it either -- for the 62-793, H inside the housing needs f at least 52 mm while H-prime inside needs f at most 25.5 mm, and the windows do not overlap, because a 4x telecentric in a 110 mm barrel is a compound telephoto-like design whose equivalent principal planes genuinely lie outside its own envelope. So fix the two groups where the hardware puts them, just inside each end of the housing, and the conjugates determine their powers exactly; above 1x the intermediate image always falls behind group 2, which therefore sees a virtual object and comes out NEGATIVE -- the telephoto pair the geometry demanded. Two consequences: the stop is the CONE and not effl over f-number (6.50 mm for the 62-793 where effl/f-number gives 0.32, wrong by twenty times), and it sits at group 1's back focal plane so the entrance pupil is infinite and the chief rays leave the object parallel. Applied only where the old route fails, so PYRITE 56/80 stays asymmetric at effl 82.39 and WWK10 stays efl-span-symmetric at 70.0315. The SPO folder now imports and its emitted groups trace paraxially to m = -4.0000, with a 2.2 mm object imaging to 8.800 mm -- the 2/3 inch sensor width its own field-of-view row quotes -- and a 15.076 mm stop that traces back to exactly f/12.5 (0792)
titles.576: a fixed-conjugate lens brings its object distance with it: flag 20260916_105357, rays seems like not focusing to sensor, on a scene holding the SPO TCL4.0X-65DI-5M. The banner read that the image forms 40.96 mm in front of the sensor with a 6.6e-12 um spot at best focus -- ideal optics, wrong conjugate. The saved rows held a 110 mm object leg, which is the WORKING DISTANCE OF THE OUTGOING 1x LENS, on a 4x lens that works at 65: tracing its own emitted groups gives magnification -0.2164 and a VIRTUAL image 16.4 mm before the rear group, which is 40.960 mm in front of the sensor and reproduces the banner exactly, where 65 mm gives -4.0000 and zero defocus. A swap preserves the object leg by design (bugs/0378) and moves the IMAGE to best focus (bugs/0388), which is right for a lens whose object distance is free and wrong for one that operates at a single point, since 45 mm outside it there is no real image for the refocus to find. bugs/0656 already places the object at the vendor working distance on a swap, but only through _lens_datasheet_wd_registration, which needs a lens STEP mesh the SPO folder does not ship AND applies the coincident-principal-plane law bugs/0792 showed is unreachable above 1x (it evaluates to -19.995 here), so the one lens that most needed its object placed was the one it could not serve. A conjugate-constrained surrogate already knows the answer -- it was built with the object at the vendor working distance and its front datum IS the housing rim -- so the model now declares it and the swap applies it when the measured route cannot: after bugs/0656 so a measurable lens keeps the measured answer, and before the refocus. The flag is deliberately narrow, set only by the conjugate-constrained build, because on the EFL route the object gap is DERIVED (the 1x WWK10's is 70.846 against a stated 110) and claiming it would move the object to a number no datasheet states (0793)
titles.577: when the vendor ships no STEP, build the envelope from the drawing: the user asked whether a STEP could be built from the PDF or DWG while the vendor's own file is awaited, because several algorithms measure against the lens BODY -- the camera-clearance clamp needs something to clear, bugs/0656's working-distance placement needs a rim to measure to, and the scene has nothing to draw. The SPO TCL4.0X-65DI-5M ships a dwg and a pdf and no STEP. Its dimension entities carry a value AND the two points it spans at 1:1 mm, so the barrel is DERIVED, not modelled by eye: axis y 184.5 where the on-axis radial dimensions centre, rim at x 181.816, and bands 0 to 54.900 at diameter 31, 54.900 to 66.500 at 34, 66.500 to 142.482 at 30, plus a diameter-16 coaxial port standing 20.5 proud at 45.561 from the rim. 54.900 + 11.600 + 75.982 = 142.482: the bands CLOSE on the body length, which is the check that they were read rather than guessed. Two rules make it trustworthy and both were found by getting them wrong first -- each on-axis radial dimension marks one band at its own station, and the port's own dimensions must not cut the profile, because the drawing's parenthesised reference to the port centre sits between the 31 and 34 callouts and taken as a step moved the first band from 54.900 to 45.561. The produced solid measures 142.482 axially, 34.0 across and 54.5 over the port, is classified by scan_lens_folder and wired by the import. It is the mechanical envelope the drawing dimensions, not the vendor's CAD, and the STEP product name says so (0794)
titles.578: the object is not an aperture: flag 20260916_113737, why the rays look so wierd, sudden bend on last two surrogate and single pencils rays reaching the sensor, not the focusing rays type. The SPO TCL4.0X-65DI-5M scene launched 0.330 mm of beam through a lens with a 26.076 mm front aperture and a 15.076 mm stop, so the stop passed 4 percent of its own diameter. _resolved_preview_pupil_radius sized that launch from two numbers that measure the wrong thing. _entrance_radius clamps to the OBJECT semi-diameter, which is a FIELD extent that says how wide the object is and never what angle the lens accepts, and at 1x and below the object is the LARGER of the two so the clamp never bound: the 1x WWK10 has 8.758 mm of object against 7.003 mm of front aperture and takes the aperture, while the 4x telecentric has 1.375 against 13.038 and took the object. Behind it PupilCalc cannot solve an object-space telecentric at all, because its entrance-pupil Newton step divides by a derivative that is identically zero when the chief ray is parallel to the axis for every object height, so it raised and the silent except left half the stop diameter, 7.538 mm, used as an aim radius at the first surface 132 mm and two groups upstream. Neither number needs guessing: aim one probe ray from the axial object point, read its height at the stop row with apertures ignored exactly as PupilCalc does, and scale, because the pupil is a paraxial construction and 0.25, 1.0 and 4.0 mm probes agree to five decimals at a 10.4000 mm aim radius, which is object NA 0.16000 equals m over 2 N_working equals 4 over 25, the datasheet working f-number recovered from the geometry. The measurement only ever RAISES the historical clamp and never past the physical front clear radius, so a scene whose object is already the wider keeps its launch to the byte, and it returns nothing for an Infinity object where the launch grid IS the pupil. It also replaces the raw half stop diameter when the declared type is STOP, which is precisely what a STOP declaration means translated to the plane the bundles aim at. The importer now declares STOP with the solved stop diameter rather than FNO, because bugs/0792 established that a conjugate-constrained build's EFL is an equivalent number with no infinite-conjugate meaning and f/12.5 against it declared a 0.824 mm pupil. The bend the flag also reported is real and is the lens: above 1x the conjugate solve returns a telephoto pair, f2 is -23.883, group 1 focuses 144.0 mm downstream which is 11.5 mm PAST group 2, and the diverging rear group takes that converging beam as a virtual object and pushes it to the sensor 22.5 mm away (0795)
titles.579: the aperture belongs to the lens, not to the scene: flag 20260916_125457 on build c771d3e7, I swapped the lens seems the rays look the same. bugs/0795 had just removed the pencil from the CLAMP and it was still coming from the DECLARATION. Driven headlessly through the real swap callback, the swap was working -- rows replaced, object at the 4x lens's own 65 mm, banner reading 4.16x, and the imported model itself declaring STOP 15.0761 -- while the SCENE stayed on the outgoing lens's FNO 12.5 and the axial bundle stayed 0.330 mm at the front datum before and after. _apply_swapped_lens_step_settings takes exactly two things from the incoming layout, the STEP path and the largest-component flag, and its docstring is explicit that everything else including source, field and pupil settings is left untouched. That is right for all of them but one: pose, object, camera, field and source describe the SCENE and the user chose them, which is why bugs/0378 and bugs/0381 exist, but an aperture describes the LENS. FNO resolves against the system EFL and after a swap that EFL is a different lens's, and EPD is a pupil diameter in millimetres which is a statement about the glass that just left. Here FNO 12.5 against the conjugate-constrained build's EQUIVALENT EFL of 10.297, which bugs/0792 showed has no infinite-conjugate meaning, resolved to a 0.824 mm entrance pupil on a lens whose stop is 15.076 mm, 18x under and exactly the pencil the user photographed twice. _apply_swapped_lens_aperture adopts the incoming declaration where the other incoming settings land, before the auto-refocus so best focus is found on the cone the lens actually passes, and returns a note so the swap says so rather than silently restating the user's aperture in another lens's terms. A declaration that says nothing -- absent, unrecognised, zero, unparseable -- is ignored and the scene's aperture left alone, and re-adopting an identical declaration is silent. The swapped scene then launches 8.320 mm where the flag traced 0.330. Measured while doing it and left for its own bug: the sensor row now reads 0.064 mm of bundle radius where a focused cone reads 0, because the 2 mm camera-clearance clamp set the rear gap to 19.526 where the lens images at 17.526, which against the MV-CS050's 3.45 um pixel is a 128 um blur disc about 37 pixels across, invisible while the launch was a pencil because a 0.022 mm beam has almost no cone to defocus (0796)
titles.580: a drawing uses the DRAWN size, not the trace mesh: flag 20260916_135706 with attachment/freecad.png, there are oversized Object Plane + Surrogate. The user exported the WWK10-110CP-111V3 scene to STEP and opened it in FreeCAD: two disc flanges punched out through a 44 mm barrel and a huge disc stood where the object plane should be. Measured against what the app drew for the same scene, the export wrote 56.009 mm for every 28.0045 mm surrogate row and 112.018 for an object plane whose own diameter is 58.539, while the aperture stop at 10.0045 and the image at 17.5161 came out correct -- which is the tell, because those are the two rows the build leaves alone. The inflation is not a defect: layout_editor._build_system_from_specs puts it there deliberately and bugs/0623/0624 states the contract in its own comment, rows between the datums REFRACT out to 2x their drawn diameter because a vendor blackbox's row diameters are paraxial bookkeeping rather than glass sizes, so a corner pencil that threads the datum and the stop must still refract instead of striking a wall -- the trace mesh extends, the DISPLAY keeps the row's drawn size, the stop keeps sole aperture authority and the datum walls remain a backstop annulus at 2x to 4x. The Object row is separately built at a computed clear aperture rather than its own diameter, which is where 112.018 equals 2 times 56.009 comes from. bugs/0674 honoured the display half of that contract for the 3D view by rescaling the runtime disc meshes; the STEP export builds its own geometry and never received it, so cad_step_export's two analytic writers revolve sdt[j] even though rows[j] is already in hand two lines above for bugs/0301's non-physical-row skip, and _collect_3d_step_export_meshes reads system.AAA directly. A drawing is sized by what is drawn: _make_occ_revolution_face takes a display_diameter override, _drawn_surface_diameter supplies row.diameter when it is a real size and None otherwise so an absent, zero or unparseable value keeps the built one, both analytic loops pass it, and the faceted fallback rescales about the mesh centre exactly as 0674 does. The trace is untouched -- SDT.Diameter still carries the 2x extension. Verified by re-exporting the real scene through both writers: object plane 112.018 to 58.539, datums and groups 56.009 to 28.005, stop and image unchanged, vendor lens and camera solids unchanged. The guard compares against the LIVE rows rather than the authored literals, because _normalize_special_rows resizes the Image row to the conjugate of the object and at 1x it becomes the object's own 58.54 (0797)
titles.581: the DXF's shapes must close: the user on their own viewport export, the DXF output there are many unclosed edges they are supposed to be closed shape, and I think this is recurring bug as well -- it is, bugs/0650 item 3 was some boxes not closed missing lines at one side not symmetry and took eight rounds. The file held 3998 polylines, none carrying the DXF closed flag, 3206 of them bare 2-vertex segments, and 90.3 percent of body polylines with a dangling end; rendered to PNG with every open end marked, there were red dots at every corner of every box. Two false starts are recorded in the bug because they cost time. The stitch tolerance is NOT the problem: the median nearest-endpoint gap of 0.0156 mm against a 1e-3 mm tolerance looked decisive and was an artifact, because instrumenting the real pipeline showed one colour bucket going 416 strips in and 120 chains out with the raw segments' median endpoint gap at 0.000000 and 66.5 percent exactly coincident -- after a correct stitch the surviving endpoints are terminal by construction, so 95 percent dangling is the expected outcome, and raising the tolerance to 0.08 mm changed nothing while producing zero extra closed shapes at any value up to 0.4. Dropping the perturbed tilts entirely moved the output only from 8050 polylines to 7748. The real causes are two. First, mesh_outline_strips unions vtkPolyDataSilhouette at three perturbed view directions so a contour lost at one tangency knife-edge is caught by a neighbour, but each tilt puts the silhouette on DIFFERENT mesh edges, so every contour arrived three times about 0.1 mm apart: 129386 mm of raw line for 46156 mm of unique geometry, and its own comment's claim that the fragment dedupe absorbs the overlap is false because that dedupe is exact. Second, merge_collinear_segments_2d emitted every result as d times t plus normal times mean_offset, a line REBUILT on the cluster's reference direction at the group's mean offset, so a segment moved even with nothing to merge with and the two arms of a corner, being in different angle clusters, moved independently: of 2854 exactly coincident endpoints in one real bucket, 13 survived, and two arms meeting exactly at (50, 0) came out at (50, 0.0125) and (50.0125, 0). Together every corner existed three times in three slightly different places, the merge chose between copies inconsistently, and the stitched chains were left a median 1.38 mm from closing -- geometry away, not tolerance away. The fix makes the perturbed passes ADDITIVE via _strips_not_already_drawn, keeping the base silhouette canonical and its connectivity untouched and admitting a perturbed fragment only where the base drew nothing near it, with a tolerance relative to the drawing's own extent so it scales with the view; and the merge unions intervals as before but emits the REAL endpoints of the members reaching each end, a group of one coming back untouched. Same scene and camera before and after: 30975 polylines to 7899, 27486 bare segments to 4666, 76 closed shapes to 149, 59502 open ends to 14294, re-rendered and eyeballed with the barrel outlines and flange circles continuous where they were dotted. Still open and written down rather than papered over: no polyline yet carries the closed flag and a profile is still several chains (0798)
titles.582: the DXF outline is a CLOSED shape, computed not assembled: bugs/0798 halved the fragmentation but left the thing the user asked for undone, they are supposed to be closed shape, with not one polyline carrying the DXF closed flag. The measurement that decided this bug is that assembling edges cannot get there: the line art is a soup of silhouette and feature edges whose graph has vertices of degree above two, T-junctions plus one contour per silhouette pass, so a greedy endpoint walk cannot know which incident edge continues a profile. Both orders were measured on real captured buckets -- merge then stitch gives 120 chains, 0 closed, 46156 mm; stitch then dedupe gives 2 chains, 0 closed, 129386 mm, walking every duplicate into two giant scribbles carrying 129386 mm of line for 46156 mm of unique geometry -- and the stitched chains ended a median 1.38 mm apart, which is geometry away rather than tolerance away. A silhouette does not have to be reconstructed from edges: project every triangle into the view plane and take the BOOLEAN UNION, whose boundary IS the outline, closed by construction, one exterior ring per connected body and one interior ring per through-hole. mesh_outline_polygons does that with shapely and lifts the 2D result back along the view direction at the mesh's own depth so the caller projects it like any other strip: measured on this scene, 11272 triangles give one closed ring of 117 vertices in 0.20 s and 231606 give one closed ring of 64 vertices in 4.47 s. The rings pass through _postprocess_layer_polylines untouched, because decomposing a finished ring into segments and re-stitching it would hand it back to the very walk that could not close it; write_dxf_r12 sets group 70 bit 1 and does not repeat the final vertex so CAD offsets, hatches and area-measures it as a region, and it does so for ANY polyline whose first vertex repeats as its last so stitched interior loops like a flange circle are flagged too; and _strips_not_already_drawn samples a sparse reference along its edges before testing coverage, since an outline ring is a handful of long edges and a fragment lying exactly on it can be half a segment from the nearest reference vertex, while the test itself moved into the VIEW PLANE because the ring sits at the mesh's mean depth and a 3D comparison measures depth rather than the drawing. Same scene and camera: polylines carrying the closed flag 0 to 105, closed outline rings 0 to 10, rendered and eyeballed with the barrel profile, coaxial port, flange circles, camera body and object-plane rectangle and disc all continuous closed loops. The ~7300 open polylines that remain are NOT duplicated outline, measured: 0 percent lie within 0.1 mm of a ring and 1.6 percent within 0.3 mm, so they are interior detail, which is open line art in any drawing (0799)
titles.583: the export draws what the VIEW shows, not what the model holds: two reports, one contract. The surrogate is hidden but the STEP output still shows the surrogate, and Show Rays is on but a fresh launch will not show rays while export STEP will, and turning it off makes the export drop them. Measured: hiding rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 gave _step_export_hidden_state frozenset 1 2 4 5 and the analytic writer still wrote 7 surfaces where 3 were expected; and on a fresh load through the app's own loader the fast-load gate _preview_trace_deferred_until_requested was True at open with 0 ray paths in the scene and show_rays_var reading True, while the export wrote 156 ray polylines, with Trace Now then giving 3249 paths. The hidden-row half is bugs/0797's shape again: _step_export_hidden_state is consulted by the mesh, edge and native-CAD collectors, but the two analytic writers in cad_step_export walk sdt[j] directly and only ever checked surf.Drawing, the row's 2D flag, and the surrogate rows are exactly what those loops write. The rays half is that _step_export_ray_polylines never read the gate and calls _trace_preview_rays itself, so it wrote rays that had never been on screen, suppressed only by the separate Show Rays check. The obvious remedy for the rays, tracing when the 3D view opens, is deliberately NOT done: bugs/0718 made that gate authoritative because the non-sequential trace runs in-process and on crashed geometry wedges in the mesh ray loop and hangs the UI with no way to interrupt it, so only a deliberate Trace Now may clear it and clearing it on open would re-open that hang. Instead both analytic writers take hidden_rows and skip those rows with export_3d_step passing _step_export_hidden_state()[0] down the analytic and native worker routes; _step_export_ray_polylines returns nothing while the gate is set so the drawing follows the view and the export stops running the very trace 0718 defers; and _pending_rays_note makes the view say rays are PENDING after a fast load, press Trace Now, on both open paths including after the STEP cache warm-up. The gate was never the problem, the silence was. Verified: 3 surfaces written, 0 rays exported while deferred, 156 after Trace Now, hidden rows seen as 1 2 4 5. The guard pins that open_3d_view does NOT clear the gate, so 0718's protection survives this fix (0800)
titles.584: the Show Rays toggle states what is on screen, and ticking it traces: the user after bugs/0800 -- if ray is not on, why not just untick the rays on, main thing here is matching UI toggle with actual scene, if user toggle rays on or off it should immediately show the ray, right now on fresh load without clicking Trace Now the rays on/off toggle is not functioning. Right on both counts and a better framing than 0800 shipped: 0800 made the view SAY that rays were pending, which is an explanation for a control that still did nothing, and a toggle that does not toggle is broken rather than merely quiet. Measured before: on a fresh load the gate was True, show_rays_var read True and there were 0 ray paths on screen, and ticking the box left all three unchanged, because _on_show_rays_changed ends in refresh_from_editor and every refresh entry honours the fast-load gate from bugs/0646 that bugs/0718 made authoritative. The fix is that TICKING THE BOX IS the deliberate trace request: bugs/0646 asks that every real trace entry clears the gate first, and bugs/0718 keeps the gate authoritative because the non-sequential trace runs in-process and can wedge the UI on crashed geometry, but a user ticking Show Rays is asking for rays in so many words exactly as Trace Now does, while an INCIDENTAL refresh still cannot clear it, which is all 0718 ever required. So _on_show_rays_changed clears the gate when the box is turned ON, never when turned off, and before refreshing; and _pending_rays_note now UNTICKS the box on a deferred open instead of leaving it lying, saying Show Rays is off because the fast load deferred the trace, tick it or press Trace Now. Verified: fresh load gives toggle False with 0 paths, ticking ON gives toggle True with 3249 paths and the gate cleared, ticking OFF hides them and leaves the gate cleared -- the box matches the scene at every point and rays appear on the tick with no Trace Now. The guard pins that neither open_3d_view nor the refresh service clears the gate, so a future just-trace-it-on-open cannot quietly reintroduce the 0718 hang (0801)
titles.585: the DXF draws only what is VISIBLE: four reports -- still have some stray lines, those strays also break one of the supposed to be closed line, the camera is also quite messy from the six-view sheet, and some lines not closed or joined -- and one cause. Three hypotheses were killed by measurement first: the collinear merge moving endpoints was already fixed and strays remained; a single-tilt export produced the identical strays to the digit so the perturbed silhouette tilts were not it; and silhouette-only and feature-only exports both produced the same strays. A fourth rule, both ends free and strictly inside an outline, matched 383 polylines or 19 percent of the drawing and when rendered would have deleted the flange circles and the camera's real detail, so it was not shipped. The export was a SEE-THROUGH wireframe projecting every edge front and back: rasterising each body's depth, 67.5 percent of the lens body's 4609 feature edges and 94.2 percent of the camera's 57903 are occluded by the body itself, and the taper strays were back-facing edges showing through the cone, inseparable from real front detail in 2D because the discriminator is DEPTH. _SceneDepthBuffer rasterises every solid in the view into one orthographic z-buffer and each body strip is cut to the runs not behind a solid, scene-wide so the lens occludes the camera and the STEP companion edge actors are tested too, in both the viewport export and the six-view sheet, on the BODIES layer only, with closed outline rings kept whole. Four details were found by getting them wrong: VTK's projection direction points INTO the scene and the first guard assumed the opposite; samples are taken ALONG segments because a long 2-point edge can pass behind a body with both ends visible; samples outside the rasterised extent are unoccluded instead of inheriting the border pixel's depth; and the test is conservative, comparing against the farthest front depth in a 3x3 neighbourhood and closing hidden gaps of two samples, because dense sampling made lines on rims flicker at pixel pitch and turned hole rims into dots and flange edges into dashes. Measured: the user's camera six-view sheet 22223 to 3900 polylines, the viewport bodies layer 7301 to 871, and lines over 5 mm 186 to 227 because the vertex-only cut had been hiding some real lines. Residuals written down: small mount-hole rims still fragment, closed-flag shapes in the viewport fall from 105 to 15 because a partly hidden loop is not a closed shape in a hidden-line drawing, and export takes about 48 s and 100 s (0802)
titles.586: a detailed part gets its own depth grid and cut specks are dropped where they are noise: follow-on to bugs/0802 whose residuals were dotted mount-hole rims on the camera six-view and coarse detail on small parts in the viewport. Two of 0802's own explanations were measured false first: the six-view depth test almost never cut a small strip at 21-35 um pixels, and returning original vertices instead of resampled points moved the sheet only 3900 to 3934. The viewport really was coarse, 263 mm of scene at 1400 px being 188 um so the camera spanned 284 px against 1396 on its sheet. An A/B of each 0802 test change on the real sheet showed gap closing does nothing measurable, the 3x3 filter removes about 1500 fragments, and sampling along segments adds about 1100 sub-0.5 mm cut pieces while recovering 21 real lines over 5 mm. Per-part tiles give a detailed body smaller than the scene its own full-resolution grid rasterising every solid overlapping it, lens 109 um and camera 40 um on the user's scene, and a truth test against a 4000 px reference cut total visible-length error from 667 mm to 282 mm and strips off by more than 0.25 mm from 406 to 144, so the viewport's 135 to 130 long lines were leaks. Dropping cut pieces under three pixels was tried against criteria set before looking: on every grid it raised the sheet's long lines 227 to 232 but cost the viewport 130 to 127, restricting it to full-resolution grids left the viewport at 127 so the loss was on tiles, and restricting it to single-part views met both, because on a sheet a cut is the part hiding itself at a rim while in a multi-body view a short piece can be a line emerging from behind another body. Result: sheet 3900 to 3192 polylines with fragments under 0.5 mm 3254 to 2532, long lines 227 to 232 and closed shapes 40 to 48; viewport bodies 871 to 664 (0803)
titles.587: an outline ring must enclose something: the user found the lens and camera six-view sheets clean but stray broken lines still inside the lens taper of the scene export, and asked why the six-view export had none. Measured on the user's own file: of 24 closed rings, 18 enclosed exactly zero area, three or four collinear points traced out and back, which is why a search over short OPEN polylines had found nothing. Earlier probes had used a camera preset named left that does not exist, silently measuring a default projection; with -yz the export matched the file at 302 body polylines and 24 closed rings, and tagging each ring's source showed bugs/0799's outline union emitting 21 rings of which 18 were zero-area while the writer's ends-meet rule contributed none. Seen from the side the tapered flank's triangles are nearly edge-on and simplifying their union at 0.02 mm collapses thin slivers into collinear points, and being flagged closed they passed whole through hidden-line removal and the post-process. The six-view sheets were clean because, parsed from the source, only the viewport collector calls mesh_outline_polygons, and the user's lens six-view file has zero zero-area rings. A ring whose mean width 2A/P is below the tolerance it was simplified to is no longer emitted. Verified in the same view: union rings 21 to 3, zero-area rings 18 to 0, closed rings 24 to 6 all real, and the taper renders clean with the rest unchanged; a flange tick and a partly drawn hole rim remain and are ordinary open lines (0804)
titles.588: the camera seats on the lens: the user swapped the SPO TCL4.0X-65DI-5M onto an MV-CS050 and asked whether the rays fanning out at the back were right. Replayed exactly (Swap Imaging Lens from Folder on the vendor folder): the swap parked the camera 2.000 mm off the lens shoulder, flange to sensor 19.526 mm on a 17.526 mm C-mount, so every bundle focused 2 mm in front of the sensor and fanned out again to it (38 um RMS, about 11 pixels) and the delivered magnification read 4.193 instead of 4.0. The post-swap refocus reserves 2 mm clearance plus the camera flange depth so a camera body is never solved into an upstream fold mirror, and its mesh layer takes the upstream row's drawn actor as the obstacle; here that row was the lens's own rear optical vertex datum, the mount face the camera screws onto, so both layers turned a seat into a 2 mm spacer. A camera right after the imaging-lens block now seats on the flange (floor = flange depth, no body clearance against a datum disc) while a camera behind a fold mirror keeps clearance plus flange. The same flag's FIELD OVERFLOWS THE SENSOR banner (field 249.3 mm) read the 60 mm default of an inspection part switched off in the scene; the overflow prediction now reads only an enabled part. Verified on the replay: flange to sensor 17.526, camera face on the shoulder, every field focused on the sensor, magnification 4.0001; old code fails A1-A6 and D1 (0806)
titles.589: the stop is where the iris is: the user found the SPO TCL4.0X-65DI-5M surrogate's rays bending suddenly outward just before the camera. bugs/0792 fixed both ideal groups 5 mm inside the housing ends; a 4x lens in a 225 mm track needs a negative telephoto rear group, and at the rear rim all of it became one 5.9 deg kink with the chief ray reaching the sensor at 7.6 deg, while the stop sat 52.1 mm behind the front face, in front of the 54.9-66.5 mm iris ring the vendor drawing labels. The DWG reader now takes the stop from the drawing itself: a LEADER labelled IRIS whose arrow tip, projected onto the housing axis (the housing dimension's front end is the one sharing an extension line with the working-distance dimension), falls inside a dimensioned ring, whose middle is the stop; and the front barrel radius from the coaxial diameter dimensions in front of it (the illumination port's diameter is measured along the axis and is not counted). The conjugate solve then pins group 1's back focal plane at the iris, which leaves a one-parameter family, and takes the member whose front group is as large as the barrel holds, the weakest rear group the housing allows: rear group 72.05 mm behind the front face, 1.20 deg of bend, 3.31 deg at the sensor, magnification, working distance, NA and image at the flange unchanged. Group and datum discs are sized to the beam each carries. A lens with no drawn stop keeps the rim placement (0807)
titles.590: the sensor rolls with the camera: the user rolled the MV-CS050 camera body 90 degrees on the TCL4.0X and asked for the FOV length by width to become width by length. Measured on the saved scene, the body turned but the FOV rectangle, the sensor rectangle and the launched 9-point field stayed landscape, because every consumer (drawn rectangles, launch field, fill-the-sensor solve, delivered FOV readouts) reads the sensor pair as the world horizontal by vertical extent and nothing read the roll. The sensor is fixed inside the camera, so the roll is honoured once at that source: the body's own X lands at the roll angle through its Rx, Ry, Rz pose (a y flip adds 180 degrees a rectangle does not see), a quarter turn swaps width and height, a non-quarter residual is reported in the HUD rather than drawn, and the HUD pairs pixel counts the same way. Every saved scene with a 90 or 270 degree roll carries a square sensor, so no existing scene changes. The same flag's FIELD REACHES THE SENSOR EDGE 0.69 mm banner was an older bug: the overflow check built its own in-plane frame with the width along Y, so a landscape field exactly filling the sensor was judged transposed; the inside test now uses the drawn frame with a rounding tolerance, while the strip frame the split-field laws use is unchanged (0808)
titles.591: a partly hidden edge is not a whole edge: the user circled a broken spot in the scene DXF where the SPO lens's illumination port meets the barrel, and noted the six-view sheet had no such problem. Reproduced headlessly (415 polylines against the user's 413, same rings, same pieces), the four 2 mm vertical ticks under the port are the walls of the flange plate's M3 holes, 1.7 mm behind the plate's front face. The depth test hid them, leaving 0.105 mm where the 3x3 min filter bleeds past the plate edge, but the viewport's hidden-line loop judged a strip fully visible by comparing POINT COUNTS: a partly hidden 2-point edge returns a 2-point run of its visible end samples, so the whole edge was kept. The six-view collector uses the runs directly, which is why it was clean. Full visibility now means the run IS the strip (same count and same end points); the loop is a helper testable without a display. The same export carried a 545 mm line far below the lens: the HUD text box, a screen-space 2D actor whose pixel quad was flattened as a body; 2D props are now skipped in both collectors. On the scene view the fix removed the hole walls of the port and both ring screws and a camera-internal board edge seen through the housing, lines over 5 mm otherwise unchanged; a one-pixel end piece at an occluder rim stays, as bugs/0803 requires in a multi-body view (0809)
titles.592: a line touching the outline is not on it: after 0809 the user's re-exported scene DXF still showed the SPO port broken, and the component six-view drew it right, the flange plate a closed rectangle. Measured on a headless export of the same view, the plate's 17 mm front bottom edge passed the depth test at full length and was then deleted by the outline dedupe, which resamples the outline ring but tested a candidate only at its vertices; both ends of that edge sit on the ring at the 0.05 mm notch floors between plate and pocket, so the whole edge counted as already drawn and the plate ends hung down to 0.14-0.19 mm stubs. The candidate is now sampled along its segments too. The four 0.105 mm ticks under the plate's top edge were the M3 hole walls 1.7 mm behind the plate face, one pixel of which the 3x3 filter calls visible beside the plate rim; at pixel pitch that tick and a real 0.25 mm peek (the bugs/0803 D fixture) are the same two samples, so a cut run of at most three samples that the raw buffer hides somewhere is kept only if the middle of one of its steps is not behind a triangle, tested on the triangles themselves. On the scene the plate closes and no tick or stub is left; lines over 5 mm 48 to 49, the camera unchanged apart from re-stitching (0811)
titles.593: a cache is a recipe: asked to fix the validation errors that kept being skipped as known, the per-phase census found 449-452 never finishing and 169, 170, 181-194 failing on missing files. 23 derived files under attachment/cad_cache, promoted-body STLs and a generated beam-splitter template referenced 132 times by 15 scenes, had been moved to the Filen trash. Loading such a scene opened the MODAL missing-assets dialog, so unattended runs hung; guards building rows without the load path lost their bodies; and the only rebuild (bugs/0021) re-meshed an overlay-promoted body in the STEP's native frame and repointed the row, face S001/F001 at x -8.84 where the scene records +12.5. The scene records each recipe: a template's name is the hash of its recorded parameters, an overlay body is the source STEP through the recorded overlay pose, cleaned and centred (resized to the recorded bounds when it was resized), and OpticalSolidFaces proves the result face by face. Rebuilt bodies are written only when every recorded face reproduces, at the recorded path, never repointed; the dialog is non-modal and redraws when closed; tools/rebuild_cad_caches.py rebuilds every scene's caches (21 rebuilt, 0 refused, 0 still missing). The overlay bodies came back bit-identical to the originals recovered from the trash; 447 and 449-452 pass, as do 169, 170, 183, 185, 186 and 189; 181 and 194 still fail on their own older assertions (0810)
titles.594: a save writes the table: the user found the om05a prism assembly haywire -- the whole B-side train, both beam-splitter far halves and both LED panels sat 8.82 mm off the authored placement every one of them carries, while the A-side rows and the same rows in the 80 mm bench read 0.000. Both files record the SAME authored centres, so re-seating them onto it is the user's "copy the prism assembly from om05a_folded_80mm.py". The first repair reported drift 0.000000 and saved a file that still held the old placement: _write_layout_file begins with _read_rows_from_table(), so rows edited in memory and saved without _sync_table() are silently overwritten by the stale table -- the trap the bugs/0591/0608 lens refit already had to comment around. Re-seated through the table the scene went from 6 of 1103 rays reaching with a 127 mm waist to 644 on-strip at 0.7 um, and the 3D scene from "no ray reaches the sensor" to an image 0.457 mm in front of it. The two big RA mirrors keep a 3.563 mm authored/live gap that is the SNAPSHOT being stale, not a displacement: the 80 mm bench images with the same live pose, and phase 505's A8b now reports that same 3.563 mm on the measured cover strip (0815)
titles.595: a slid row says so: bugs/0769 split a leg in the user's om05a scene (RA mirror 2's 45.13 -> 36.31 plus an 8.82 mm sensor standoff), preserved the sum AT THE SENSOR and recorded "nothing moves" -- but seven free-placed prism rows sat BETWEEN the row that lost the 8.82 mm and the row that gained it, so their station and their world z dropped by exactly that, and the scene traced 6 rays of 1103 until the user looked at it and said the prisms were off centre. Nothing in the app had said a word, although the bugs/0750 audit has had the instrument since: its DELTA form is silent on an unmoved scene and on a merely stale snapshot (om05a's own 3.563 mm from bugs/0760), so it can run on every model change. It now does -- _apply_model_change takes a reading before the redraw, refresh_scene makes the painted scene the next baseline (both the sync and the async trace), and the rows that moved ride the solve banner. The notice REPORTS: a promoted row is usually vendor hardware and where it sits is the user's, so nothing is moved back for them, and a row that returns to its seat clears its own notice at the next paint (0816)
titles.596: a seat that moved on purpose can be re-recorded: StepOverlayPromotion.center_world is written once, at promotion, so bugs/0760's deliberate move -- the big om05a RA mirror seated 3.563 mm out onto the 7.596 mm clearance measured on the production assembly, against the 4.033 mm the scene had -- left a snapshot nothing could refresh, and the bugs/0750 audit, the bugs/0816 notice and the authored cover strips have all been 3.563 mm behind ever since (phase 505's A8b still reports it). A promoted row's right-click, on the canvas and in the Scene Components tree, now offers 'Pin Current Placement as Authored' with the amount in the label, and only on a row that is actually off its seat; it shows both poses, records the LIVE one on the user's say-so and keeps the old one as center_world_repinned_from. It MOVES NOTHING -- thickness, decentres, tilts and the live pose are untouched, which is the whole point on vendor hardware -- and it is never automatic (0817)
titles.597: the Show Rays box states the scene on EVERY path: the user, after 0801 -- "I still see Rays ON is tick but no rays is actually on. I have to untick and tick to make it work. I randomly open .py files." 0801 made the box match the scene and unticked it in open_3d_view; measured, two paths kept the tick anyway. The 3D-session sidecar restores the SAVED overlay toggles at the START of every refresh_from_editor, and om05a_folded.open3d.json carries show_rays_var true, so the box the open path had just cleared was re-ticked by the very refresh that followed it (measured on a fresh open, settled past the STEP cache warm-up: ticked True, gate True, 0 ray actors); and loading another .py into an already-open inspector never runs the open path at all, leaving the same lie after every load. The rule now lives at the PAINTER, where the session restore no longer gets the last word and every present and future refresh entry inherits it, and _pending_rays_note delegates to it instead of repeating it. It can only turn the box OFF -- asking for rays stays the user's, and ticking is still the deliberate request that clears the bugs/0646 gate and traces, which bugs/0718 requires. Measured after: open gives ticked False with 0 actors, ONE tick gives ticked True with 12 actors and the gate cleared, an ordinary repaint keeps them, unticking hides them, and a load into the open window leaves the box off rather than lying (0818)
titles.598: the surrogate draws the vendor's glass, not its barrel: the user flagged machine_vision_120mm_65M.py as "lens surrogate oversized" -- its Front/Rear Optical Vertex Datum discs were drawn at 46.0 mm and the Blackbox groups at 38.0 mm against a PYRITE 5.6/120 STEP whose visible glass measures 30.39 mm inside a 46 mm collar. bugs/0703 taught the folder import to size discs from the measured glass and it still does (the same folder imports at 30.3906 today), but nothing could reach a scene already built: this one descends from machine_vision_120mm_pyrite_datasheet_1x.py, a July layout with 46.0 and 38.0 hard-coded. The lens STEP's right-click now offers 'Refit Surrogate Glass to Vendor STEP (46 -> 30.39 mm)...', and only when the discs really are wider; it shrinks the block onto the measured glass, never touches the aperture stop, never goes below it and never enlarges, so a narrower disc the user drew stays theirs. Measured on the flagged scene: four rows 46/38 -> 30.3906 with the 21.55 mm stop untouched and the ray count unchanged at 189 -- the prescription does not move, only how wide the glass is DRAWN, and with it the vendor's own vignette (0819)
titles.599: a lens surface is an ELEMENT, not one face of it: bugs/0819 reported that the ELS-85's glass could not be measured, and the user asked whether the vendor STEP was missing an element. It is not. The vendor splits one lens surface across several spherical faces and _step_glass_aperture measured a FACE: the ELS-85 carries each element as two half-caps, both with extents [2.657, 28.058, 14.158] and both on the sphere centred [17.006, -2.417, 54.0], so the reader took 14.158 mm for an element 28.058 mm across -- on an 85 mm f/4.5 lens whose pupil alone is 18.889 mm, which is how the fragment gave itself away. The 150 mm 15056 splits its steeply curved elements four ways (18.596 -> 26.624) and the 0.75X telecentric two ways (14.893 -> 29.643). Faces are now grouped by the sphere they lie on (centre and radius) and each element measured on the union of its faces; a face with no sphere parameters is still its own element and the area gate still drops a small protective cap. Measured across all 22 vendor lens STEPs, only those three change -- the PYRITE bodies, whose elements are one face each, and the ball lens, whose single hemisphere IS its glass, read exactly as before (0820)
titles.600: the 7-row penta cascade is derived, not stored: the user retired the five_penta fixtures -- "we only need five_penta_prism_analytic_telescope_cascade.py" -- and the one the whole suite loads was among them, which phase 0 hard-fails without and six other modules read. Measured, the user was right that the analytic file 'got more': it carries 18 rows to the plain cascade's 7 and its first six, Object plus Penta prism 1..5, are BYTE-IDENTICAL; the only difference is the tail, where the plain file stops at an Image row at the origin and the analytic one continues into ball lenses, a DCV, an achromat and a cylindrical. So the plain cascade is the analytic one's prism head plus that Image row, and keeping both stored the same geometry twice. ensure_five_penta_cascade derives it through the editor's own writer when it is missing, phase 0 and the five standalone consumers ensure before they judge, and the file is untracked. Verified by deleting it: the suite regenerated it and phases 0-60 passed exactly as with the stored fixture (60 pass, only the baseline-known phase 52 red), with the derived rows matching the source field for field (0821)
titles.601: an illumination map that is mostly shot noise SAYS SO: the bin rule min(max(24, sqrt(N)*3), 128) grows the grid as fast as the samples, so hits-per-bin stays near 1 at any ray budget and every feature is Poisson noise. Measured on the real MV-150 coaxial-LED scene at its shipped 8000 rays, the 2-D heatmap lands at 1.17 hits per lit bin (92.6% relative error, ~343x more rays needed for 5%) while penta 175's 1-D strip profile gets 19.6 hits/bin (22.6% error) against a 0.617 edge/centre dip -- so the dark edges ARE real but that map could never have shown them, and bugs/0596 had already reached the same verdict by hand on another scene (294 hits, 16x16 grid, ~1.1 hits/bin) after two candidate fixes left every metric byte-identical. The map now carries UNWEIGHTED per-bin counts beside the power histogram (huge per-bin power must not buy a sparse map a pass), and the report leads with a sampling verdict naming the ray count a 5%-error map needs, plus a flux ledger closing input-hit-missed on power and launched-hit-missed on rays. A clean result still prints its numbers: silence means nothing was measured (0822)
titles.602: the app names the overlay family instead of the user guessing: three object-plane overlay families scale to the same field semi-diagonal and TWO draw the byte-identical green (0.2,0.9,0.35) 0.02 apart in opacity (QE pick disc 0.10, Det pick fill 0.08), while the third -- reference surfaces -- takes its opacity from the scene bundle's mesh opacity and has NO literal at all, which is why bugs/0659 round 1 blamed it for a disc it does not draw. overlay_registry declares each family's colour, opacity, shapes, toggle var, UI paths, owning module and actor lifecycle; identify_overlay never excludes a family by a literal it does not declare (excluding it IS the 0659 mistake, automated), overlay_clash_report names every shared colour and what separates it, and verify_registry_against_source re-reads the literals from their real modules so a drift fails here instead of turning the registry into the next stale note. Shape rules OUT the rectangle-drawer rather than narrowing to one family -- the reference disc is a disc too (0823)
titles.603: which rays get DRAWN depends on the ray, not its position: the illumination overlay capped with rng.choice(len(polylines), cap) -- a draw over LIST POSITIONS that its own comment called deterministic, and is, for one fixed list. Across runs anything that changed the list re-rolled every ray on screen: a different ray budget, a role tag that now matches (the 20260708_1516..1519 fallback swaps the whole input), one more ray clipping short, or any upstream RNG consumption -- on exactly the path a user reaches for to find where stray light came from. Selection is now a pure function of (ray identity, seed) through a splitmix64 finalizer, keyed on the engine's source_ray_index and never on position. Precisely: order-independent, RNG-decoupled and reproducible at a fixed population, but NOT population-independent under smallest-k -- select_by_probability is the policy for comparing two budgets, and the first draft of the comment overclaimed this and was corrected. _split now carries (record, polyline) pairs while the aperture statistics keep reading the FULL populations (0824)
titles.604: one shared shape for 'this number should not be believed': fifteen report surfaces had no common way to say a result is untrustworthy, and saying nothing looked identical to passing. result_diagnostics encodes three rules that each already cost a bug -- an empty finding list renders 'Nothing was measured. This is NOT a clean result' rather than silence (0822); a WARNING with an empty remedy is REFUSED AT CONSTRUCTION citing 0777, which shipped 'move the device stage / camera focus to land it' for a blur no move could shrink, with NO_REMEDY the way to state that nothing can be done and have it counted and printed; and warnings render above info with the count as the first line. illumination_findings re-expresses the 0822 verdicts under stable dotted codes while illumination_diagnostic_lines is untouched so no existing reader shifts, asserted here rather than assumed. The undersampling remedy now also offers binning coarser, which the MV-150 rebin sweep showed reads 13.3% error at 32 bins against 49.7% at the auto 128 on the same data (0825)
titles.605: Scene IR Phase A -- lower a scene to flat data and read it from NOWHERE: Step 2 of the earlier design stalled because nobody could find the producer of the drawn geometry (one patch inert, both curve builders and every _compute_*_layout_geometry* wrapped and none fired while twelve row actors drew), so Phase A builds the instrument that can state what every consumer believes and moves nothing. It found the design's uniform-anchor assumption was wrong on half the gate set: ELS85 declares ScenePlacement.anchor='row_pose' on 3 rows while om05a_folded has NO anchors and NO placement offsets yet resolves 11 bodies at 0.0000 mm through the output-port graph -- two mechanisms, differently shaped. ELS85's declared mechanism cannot be reconstructed (center_world is not row pose + placement_offset_xyz; that offset's z equals bounds_min_world's z), so those bodies fall back and SAY so. to_world carries a frame tag because world_pose does not fold, and is_fully_post_fold() is asserted FALSE -- a guard that passed today would measure nothing, and it turns green at Phase D (0826)
titles.606: the preview ray count costs N SQUARED and the UI never said so: measured on the user's own 25.7-minute om05a session, 16 traces cost 448 s, one lens swap cost 150 s, and 91% of all bundle time was 78 bundles x 361 rays -- while all nine scene refreshes together cost 31 s, so rendering was never the cost.
